Gender Data is data regarding the relationship of relations in status, roles, and conditions between men and women. 31. Gender and Child Data System is the institutionalization of the implementation of Gender and Child Data consisting of components of regulations, institutions, and mechanisms in ministries/agencies and regions in the context of planning, implementation, evaluation, and reporting of results of policies/programs/activities of Gender Responsive and Child-caring development. 32. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a straight line up or down to the third degree. 33. Family Quality is the condition of the Family determined by the dimensions of quality of legality and structure, quality of physical resilience, quality of economic resilience, quality of socio-psychological resilience, and quality of socio-cultural resilience in realizing Gender Equality and Child's Rights. 34. Violence is any action that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, mentally, psychologically, including intimidation, forced eviction, threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, neglect and preventing the ability to enjoy all rights and freedoms. 35. Violence Against Women hereinafter abbreviated as KTP is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, and psychologically, including threats of certain actions, arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the private or public sphere. 36. Violence Against Children hereinafter abbreviated as KTA is any act against a Child that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of freedom. 37. Domestic Violence hereinafter abbreviated as KDRT is any act against a person, especially women, that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically, and/or household neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of freedom within the household sphere. 38. Discrimination is any restriction, harassment, or exclusion that is directly or indirectly based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, group, class, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs, which results in reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural and other aspects of life. 39. Exploitation is an action with or without the victim's consent which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or service, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial. 40. Witness and/or Victim is a witness who is also a victim who experiences psychological, mental, physical, sexual, economic, and/or social suffering, caused by the criminal act of human trafficking. 41. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or adoptive mother. 42. Guardian is a person or body who in fact exercises custody as a Parent over a Child. 43. Business World is micro enterprises, small enterprises, medium enterprises, and large enterprises that conduct economic activities in Indonesia and are domiciled in Indonesia. 44. Community is individuals, families, groups, mass media, business world, and social organizations and/or community organizations. 45. Community Participation is the participation of community members to channel their aspirations, thoughts, and interests in the administration of Regional Government. 46. Community Organization hereinafter referred to as Ormas is an organization established and formed by the community voluntarily based on common aspirations, will, needs, interests, activities, and goals to participate in development for the achievement of the objectives of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia based on Pancasila and the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. 47. Social Conflict hereinafter referred to as Conflict is a feud and/or physical clash with Violence between two or more community groups that lasts for a certain time and has a broad impact resulting in insecurity and social disintegration thus disrupting national stability and hindering national development. 48. Paragraph (1)
Point a
What is meant by "Children in Emergency Situations" are Children who are in environmental situations that threaten and disrupt the life and livelihood of Children caused by natural, non-natural, and/or social factors.

Point b
What is meant by "Children in Conflict with the Law" are Children in conflict with the law, Children who are victims of criminal acts, and Children who are witnesses to criminal acts.

Point c
What is meant by "Children from Minority and Isolated Groups" are Children who are left behind, at the forefront, outermost in environments with different cultures, traditions, ethnicities, races, religions from other children whose numbers are far fewer than Children of other groups.

Point d
What is meant by "Children Who Are Economically Exploited" are Children who are victims of acts of prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or abilities of Children by other parties or other similar actions to obtain material benefits.

What is meant by "Children Who Are Sexually Exploited" are Children who are exploited to obtain benefits through sexual organs or other body organs of Children, including but not limited to all prostitution and indecency activities.

Point e
What is meant by "Children Who Are Victims of Narcotics, Alcohol, Psychotropic, and Other Addictive Substances Abuse" are Children who are persuaded, deceived, tricked, forced, and/or threatened to use narcotics, alcohol, psychotropics, and other addictive substances.

Point f
What is meant by "Children Who Are Victims of Pornography" are Children who experience trauma or suffering as a result of pornography crimes.

Point g
What is meant by "Children with HIV and AIDS" are Children who are infected with HIV and/or AIDS either transmitted from parents or from other risk factors.

Point h
What is meant by "Child Victims of Kidnapping" are Children who are taken by someone unlawfully with the intention of placing the Child under their power or the power of others or to place the Child in a helpless state.

What is meant by "Child Victims of Sale" are Children who are transferred by a person or group of people to other parties for compensation or other reasons.

What is meant by "Child Victims of Trafficking" are Children who experience psychological, mental, physical, sexual, economic, and/or social suffering resulting from acts of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt with threats of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether conducted within the country or internationally, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the Child being exploited.

Point i
What is meant by "Child Victims of Physical Violence" are Children who experience violence that causes pain, illness, or serious injury.

What is meant by "Child Victims of Psychological Violence" are Children who experience fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness, and/or severe psychological suffering.

Point j
What is meant by "Child Victims of Sexual Crimes" are Children who experience forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural and/or unwanted manner, and forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or specific purposes.

Point k
What is meant by "Child Victims of Terrorism Networks" are Children who experience physical, mental suffering, and/or economic loss caused by terrorism crimes whether as child victims, child perpetrators, children of perpetrators, and child witnesses.

Point 1
What is meant by "Children with Disabilities" are Children who experience physical, intellectual, mental, and/or sensory limitations over a long period of time who in interacting with the environment may experience obstacles and difficulties to participate fully and effectively based on equal rights.

Point m
What is meant by "Child Victims of Maltreatment" are Children who are threatened physically and non-physically due to acts of violence, treated wrongly or improperly in the family environment or closest social environment, so that their basic needs are not properly fulfilled either physically, spiritually, or socially.

Point n
What is meant by "Child Victims of Maltreatment" are Children who are threatened physically and non-physically due to acts of violence, treated wrongly or improperly in the family environment or closest social environment, so that their basic needs are not properly fulfilled either physically, spiritually, or socially.

What is meant by Child Victims of Neglect are Children who do not receive fulfillment of needs such as but not limited to health, security, and welfare needs from parents or other persons who have legal responsibility to care for the Child resulting in harm to the Child's growth and development process.

Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 27. Special Protection is a form of protection received by Children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger themselves and their lives in their development. 28. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency Area with a development system that guarantees the Fulfillment of Child's Rights and Special Protection of Children carried out in a planned, comprehensive, and sustainable manner. 29.

I. GENERAL

Women and children have an important and strategic role in efforts to support development and the administration of regional government, however in reality the position of women and children in social, national and state life is still positioned as a group vulnerable to various forms of violence and/or threats of violence as well as other discriminatory treatment.

Women's Empowerment and Child Protection constitute the main pillars in efforts to improve the quality of reliable human resources in the future, by instilling and implementing the values of gender equality, and the implementation of the fulfillment of the rights of women and children, as well as enhancing the role and position of women and children in efforts to support the administration of government and development in the Region.

In the context of administering regional government affairs, women's empowerment and child protection, and improvement of family quality in the Sumedang Regency Area, is essentially one of the implementations of the administration of concurrent government affairs which are the authority of the Sumedang Regency Area in the field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

The Policy on Women's Empowerment and Protection, Child Protection, and Family Quality Improvement in the Sumedang Regency Area is implemented by involving and/or being supported by all components of society and stakeholders in the Sumedang Regency Area from various sectors of community life, and every program and activity is carried out comprehensively, in an integrated, sustainable, and continuous manner, as well as in synergy with national policies and programs in the field of women's empowerment and protection, child protection and family quality improvement.

To provide guarantees of legal certainty and legal protection as well as to realize effectiveness, efficiency, optimization, accountability, transparency, and administrative order as well as to serve as a guideline in the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection in the Sumedang Regency Area, it is necessary to regulate and stipulate by Regional Regulation.

Article 39

1. Prevention of KTP involving parties in the Regency Area as referred to in Article 37 letter a, shall be implemented in accordance with standards and procedures.
2. Standards for prevention of KTP as referred to in paragraph (1) shall include:
a. institutional implementers of KTP prevention in the Regency Area;
b. understanding of KTP; and
c. integration of KTP prevention policies in all development sectors.
3. Procedures for prevention of KTP as referred to in paragraph (1) shall include:
a. coordination and synchronization of implementation of policies, programs, and activities for KTP prevention in the Regency Area, consisting of:
1\. issuing regulations on KTP prevention involving parties in the Regency Area, covering primary, secondary, and tertiary prevention;
2\. socialization and advocacy on KTP to policy makers and other stakeholders in the Regency Area; and
3\. establishing cooperation for KTP prevention involving parties in the Regency Area.  b. policy advocacy and service assistance for Women's Protection in the Regency Area, covering:
1\. building commitment in KTP prevention;
2\. integrating KTP prevention into the Regency regional development planning; and
3\. encouraging enhancement of Community Participation and cooperation with Business Sector and mass media in KTP prevention.

Article 72

1. Prevention of VAC involving parties in the Regency Area as referred to in Article 70 letter a shall be implemented in accordance with standards and procedures.
2. Standards for the prevention of VAC involving parties in the Regency Area as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
3. Procedures for the prevention of VAC involving parties in the Regency Area as referred to in paragraph (1) shall consist of:
a. development and strengthening of institutional arrangements for VAC prevention;
b. policy advocacy and assistance or technical guidance on the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for VAC prevention in the Regency Area; and
c. coordination and synchronization of VAC prevention in the Regency Area.

I. GENERAL

Women and children have an important and strategic role in efforts to support development and the administration of regional government, however in reality the position of women and children in social, national and state life is still positioned as a group vulnerable to various forms of violence and/or threats of violence as well as other discriminatory treatment.

Women's Empowerment and Child Protection constitute the main pillars in efforts to improve the quality of reliable human resources in the future, by instilling and implementing the values of gender equality, and the implementation of the fulfillment of the rights of women and children, as well as enhancing the role and position of women and children in efforts to support the administration of government and development in the Region.

In the context of administering regional government affairs, women's empowerment and child protection, and improvement of family quality in the Sumedang Regency Area, is essentially one of the implementations of the administration of concurrent government affairs which are the authority of the Sumedang Regency Area in the field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

The Policy on Women's Empowerment and Protection, Child Protection, and Family Quality Improvement in the Sumedang Regency Area is implemented by involving and/or being supported by all components of society and stakeholders in the Sumedang Regency Area from various sectors of community life, and every program and activity is carried out comprehensively, in an integrated, sustainable, and continuous manner, as well as in synergy with national policies and programs in the field of women's empowerment and protection, child protection and family quality improvement.

To provide guarantees of legal certainty and legal protection as well as to realize effectiveness, efficiency, optimization, accountability, transparency, and administrative order as well as to serve as a guideline in the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection in the Sumedang Regency Area, it is necessary to regulate and stipulate by Regional Regulation.

I. GENERAL

Women and children have an important and strategic role in efforts to support development and the administration of regional government, however in reality the position of women and children in social, national and state life is still positioned as a group vulnerable to various forms of violence and/or threats of violence as well as other discriminatory treatment.

Women's Empowerment and Child Protection constitute the main pillars in efforts to improve the quality of reliable human resources in the future, by instilling and implementing the values of gender equality, and the implementation of the fulfillment of the rights of women and children, as well as enhancing the role and position of women and children in efforts to support the administration of government and development in the Region.

In the context of administering regional government affairs, women's empowerment and child protection, and improvement of family quality in the Sumedang Regency Area, is essentially one of the implementations of the administration of concurrent government affairs which are the authority of the Sumedang Regency Area in the field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

The Policy on Women's Empowerment and Protection, Child Protection, and Family Quality Improvement in the Sumedang Regency Area is implemented by involving and/or being supported by all components of society and stakeholders in the Sumedang Regency Area from various sectors of community life, and every program and activity is carried out comprehensively, in an integrated, sustainable, and continuous manner, as well as in synergy with national policies and programs in the field of women's empowerment and protection, child protection and family quality improvement.

To provide guarantees of legal certainty and legal protection as well as to realize effectiveness, efficiency, optimization, accountability, transparency, and administrative order as well as to serve as a guideline in the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection in the Sumedang Regency Area, it is necessary to regulate and stipulate by Regional Regulation.

I. GENERAL

Women and children have an important and strategic role in efforts to support development and the administration of regional government, however in reality the position of women and children in social, national and state life is still positioned as a group vulnerable to various forms of violence and/or threats of violence as well as other discriminatory treatment.

Women's Empowerment and Child Protection constitute the main pillars in efforts to improve the quality of reliable human resources in the future, by instilling and implementing the values of gender equality, and the implementation of the fulfillment of the rights of women and children, as well as enhancing the role and position of women and children in efforts to support the administration of government and development in the Region.

In the context of administering regional government affairs, women's empowerment and child protection, and improvement of family quality in the Sumedang Regency Area, is essentially one of the implementations of the administration of concurrent government affairs which are the authority of the Sumedang Regency Area in the field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

The Policy on Women's Empowerment and Protection, Child Protection, and Family Quality Improvement in the Sumedang Regency Area is implemented by involving and/or being supported by all components of society and stakeholders in the Sumedang Regency Area from various sectors of community life, and every program and activity is carried out comprehensively, in an integrated, sustainable, and continuous manner, as well as in synergy with national policies and programs in the field of women's empowerment and protection, child protection and family quality improvement.

To provide guarantees of legal certainty and legal protection as well as to realize effectiveness, efficiency, optimization, accountability, transparency, and administrative order as well as to serve as a guideline in the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection in the Sumedang Regency Area, it is necessary to regulate and stipulate by Regional Regulation.

CHAPTER III PROTECTION OF WOMEN

Part One General

Article 21

1. The Regency Regional Government has the authority to administer the protection of women's rights in the Regency.
2. The administration of protection of women's rights in the Regency as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be implemented by the Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

I. GENERAL

Women and children have an important and strategic role in efforts to support development and the administration of regional government, however in reality the position of women and children in social, national and state life is still positioned as a group vulnerable to various forms of violence and/or threats of violence as well as other discriminatory treatment.

Women's Empowerment and Child Protection constitute the main pillars in efforts to improve the quality of reliable human resources in the future, by instilling and implementing the values of gender equality, and the implementation of the fulfillment of the rights of women and children, as well as enhancing the role and position of women and children in efforts to support the administration of government and development in the Region.

In the context of administering regional government affairs, women's empowerment and child protection, and improvement of family quality in the Sumedang Regency Area, is essentially one of the implementations of the administration of concurrent government affairs which are the authority of the Sumedang Regency Area in the field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

The Policy on Women's Empowerment and Protection, Child Protection, and Family Quality Improvement in the Sumedang Regency Area is implemented by involving and/or being supported by all components of society and stakeholders in the Sumedang Regency Area from various sectors of community life, and every program and activity is carried out comprehensively, in an integrated, sustainable, and continuous manner, as well as in synergy with national policies and programs in the field of women's empowerment and protection, child protection and family quality improvement.

To provide guarantees of legal certainty and legal protection as well as to realize effectiveness, efficiency, optimization, accountability, transparency, and administrative order as well as to serve as a guideline in the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection in the Sumedang Regency Area, it is necessary to regulate and stipulate by Regional Regulation.

Part Two Obligations and Responsibilities

Article 51

1. The Regency Regional Government, Community, Family, and Parents or Guardians have obligations and responsibilities for the administration of Child Protection in the Regency Area.
2. The obligations and responsibilities of the Regency Regional Government in implementing the administration of Child Protection in the Regency Area as referred to in paragraph (1), include:
a. respecting the Fulfillment of Children's Rights without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race, class, gender, ethnicity, culture and language, legal status, birth order, and physical and/or mental condition;
b. implementing and supporting national policies in the administration of Child protection in the Regency Area; and
c. providing support for facilities, infrastructure, and availability of human resources in the administration of Child Protection in the Regency Area.
3. The Regency Regional Government in carrying out obligations and responsibilities in Child Protection in the Regency Area as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2), shall be implemented by:
a. guaranteeing the protection, care, and welfare of Children with due regard to the rights and obligations of Parents, Guardians, or other persons who are legally responsible for the Child; and
b. supervising the implementation of the administration of Child Protection in the Regency Area.

I. GENERAL

Women and children have an important and strategic role in efforts to support development and the administration of regional government, however in reality the position of women and children in social, national and state life is still positioned as a group vulnerable to various forms of violence and/or threats of violence as well as other discriminatory treatment.

Women's Empowerment and Child Protection constitute the main pillars in efforts to improve the quality of reliable human resources in the future, by instilling and implementing the values of gender equality, and the implementation of the fulfillment of the rights of women and children, as well as enhancing the role and position of women and children in efforts to support the administration of government and development in the Region.

In the context of administering regional government affairs, women's empowerment and child protection, and improvement of family quality in the Sumedang Regency Area, is essentially one of the implementations of the administration of concurrent government affairs which are the authority of the Sumedang Regency Area in the field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

The Policy on Women's Empowerment and Protection, Child Protection, and Family Quality Improvement in the Sumedang Regency Area is implemented by involving and/or being supported by all components of society and stakeholders in the Sumedang Regency Area from various sectors of community life, and every program and activity is carried out comprehensively, in an integrated, sustainable, and continuous manner, as well as in synergy with national policies and programs in the field of women's empowerment and protection, child protection and family quality improvement.

To provide guarantees of legal certainty and legal protection as well as to realize effectiveness, efficiency, optimization, accountability, transparency, and administrative order as well as to serve as a guideline in the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection in the Sumedang Regency Area, it is necessary to regulate and stipulate by Regional Regulation.

I. GENERAL

Women and children have an important and strategic role in efforts to support development and the administration of regional government, however in reality the position of women and children in social, national and state life is still positioned as a group vulnerable to various forms of violence and/or threats of violence as well as other discriminatory treatment.

Women's Empowerment and Child Protection constitute the main pillars in efforts to improve the quality of reliable human resources in the future, by instilling and implementing the values of gender equality, and the implementation of the fulfillment of the rights of women and children, as well as enhancing the role and position of women and children in efforts to support the administration of government and development in the Region.

In the context of administering regional government affairs, women's empowerment and child protection, and improvement of family quality in the Sumedang Regency Area, is essentially one of the implementations of the administration of concurrent government affairs which are the authority of the Sumedang Regency Area in the field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

The Policy on Women's Empowerment and Protection, Child Protection, and Family Quality Improvement in the Sumedang Regency Area is implemented by involving and/or being supported by all components of society and stakeholders in the Sumedang Regency Area from various sectors of community life, and every program and activity is carried out comprehensively, in an integrated, sustainable, and continuous manner, as well as in synergy with national policies and programs in the field of women's empowerment and protection, child protection and family quality improvement.

To provide guarantees of legal certainty and legal protection as well as to realize effectiveness, efficiency, optimization, accountability, transparency, and administrative order as well as to serve as a guideline in the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection in the Sumedang Regency Area, it is necessary to regulate and stipulate by Regional Regulation.

Article 73

1. Prevention of VAC involving parties in the Regency Area as referred to in Article 70 letter a shall be measured using criteria.

Article 39

c. monitoring; and

a. institutional;
b. human resources;
c. availability of communication, information, and education materials; and
d. synergy and coordination.

a. policy advocacy and assistance for development of Service Provider Institutions for Improving Family Quality in the Regency Area;
b. capacity building of resources of Service Provider Institutions for Improving Family Quality in the Regency Area; and
c. strengthening networks among Service Provider Institutions for Improving Family Quality in the Regency Area.

Article 84

1. Improvement of Family Quality in realizing Gender Equality and Children's Rights in the Regency Area, is implemented in accordance with standards and procedures.
2. Standards for improving Family Quality as referred to in paragraph (1) include:
a. institutional;
b. availability of communication, information, education materials;
c. synergy and coordination; and
d. monitoring, evaluation, and reporting.

a. policy advocacy and family assistance to realize Gender Equality and Children's Rights in the Regency Area include:
1\. preparation of planning and budgeting documents for Family Quality that realize Gender Equality and Children's Rights;
2\. coordination and synchronization of policy formulation for Family Quality that realizes Gender Equality and Children's Rights;
3\. increasing Community Participation and mass media in improving Family Quality that realizes Gender Equality and Children's Rights; and

b. implementation of communication, information, and education on Gender Equality and Children's Rights for Families in the Regency Area; and
c. development of Community activities for improving Family Quality in the Regency Area.

Article 97

1. The community may participate in the administration of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection in the Regency Region.
2. Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) is conducted by:
a. individual Indonesian Citizens;
b. community groups; and/or
c. Community Organizations.
3. Community Participation as referred to in paragraph (1), is facilitated by the Regency Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.
4. Facilitation in Community Participation as referred to in paragraph (1), by establishing public participation forums for the welfare of women and Children, Puspaga, community-based integrated child protection, Children's Forum, federation of women's organizations, sekoper cinta, and women heads of household in the Regency Region.
5. Further provisions regarding Community Participation and Community Participation Facilities in the administration of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection in the Regency Region as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2), are regulated in a Regent Regulation.

Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a straight line up or down to the third degree. 33. Discrimination is any restriction, harassment, or exclusion that is directly or indirectly based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, group, class, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs, which results in reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural and other aspects of life. 39. Exploitation is an action with or without the victim's consent which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or service, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial. 40. Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Regency Area is the Regency Area of Sumedang. 2. Regency Regional Government is the Regent as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 3. Regency Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and the Regional House of Representatives in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of the Region. 4. Regent is the Regent of Sumedang. 5. Regional Secretary is the Regional Secretary of Sumedang Regency. 6. Gender is the values, roles, and responsibilities of women and men that are socially and culturally constructed by society. 7. Gender Perspective is a point of view to understand and analyze the values, roles, and responsibilities of women and men that are socially and culturally constructed by society. 8. Gender Responsive is consistent and systematic attention to respond to the needs, problems, aspirations, and experiences of women and men aimed at realizing Gender Equality. 9. Gender Responsive Planning and Budgeting hereinafter abbreviated as PPRG is a systematic effort to integrate Gender into planning and budgeting. 10. Gender Mainstreaming hereinafter abbreviated as PUG is a strategy to realize Gender Equality, through the integration of Gender Perspective into regional development. 11. Gender Equality is an equal condition and position between women and men to obtain their rights as human beings through a fair process in accessing and controlling resources, actively participating, and obtaining benefits from regional development. 12. Disaggregated Data is data by sex, status and condition of women and men in all fields of Development including health, education, economy and employment, political field, legal field, social field, cultural field, decision making and violence. 13. Access is the capacity to use resources to fully participate actively and productively (socially, economically and politically) in society including Access to resources, services, labor and employment, information and benefits. 14. Participation is the involvement of a person/group both physically, mentally and spiritually in an activity and or in decision making. 15. Benefit is the usefulness of resources that can be enjoyed optimally!
16. Village is a legal community unit that has territorial boundaries authorized to regulate and manage government affairs, the interests of the local community based on community initiative, rights of origin and/or traditional rights that are recognized and respected in the Government System of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia. 17. Women's Empowerment is an effort to obtain access and control over economic, political, social, and cultural resources, so that women can organize themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and actively participate in solving problems, so as to be able to build capacity and self-concept. 18. Women's Protection is all efforts aimed at protecting and providing a sense of security to women and fulfilling their rights through consistent, structured, and systematic attention aimed at achieving Gender Equality. 19. Quality of Life of Women is an effort to improve the physical and mental condition of women in fulfilling their rights and life needs as part of human rights from various fields of development, especially education, health, economy, science and technology, socio-culture, politics, law, and the environment. 20. Institutionalization of PUG is the process of institutionalizing PUG into a sustainable system to achieve equality between women and men at all levels of government. 21. PUG Working Group hereinafter referred to as Pokja PUG is a consultation forum for implementers and movers of PUG from various agencies and institutions. 22. Gender-Based Violence hereinafter abbreviated as KBG is a violation of human rights caused by roles and labeling based on sex, which denies human dignity and the right to oneself that has an impact on, or has an impact similar to physical, psychological, and sexual or brings suffering to women and children including all forms of actions, coercion, arbitrariness and deprivation of freedom, carried out in the public sphere or private life. 23. Child is a person who is not yet 18 (eighteen) years old, including a child who is still in the womb. 24. Child's Rights are part of human rights that must be guaranteed, protected, and fulfilled by Parents, Family, community, state, government, and regional government. 25. Fulfillment of Child's Rights is an effort to fulfill the human rights of Children by taking legislative, administrative, budgetary, legal actions, and other actions to ensure that Children obtain civil rights and freedoms, family environment and alternative care rights, basic health and welfare rights, as well as education rights, leisure time utilization, and cultural activities. 26. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 27. Special Protection is a form of protection received by Children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger themselves and their lives in their development. 28. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency Area with a development system that guarantees the Fulfillment of Child's Rights and Special Protection of Children carried out in a planned, comprehensive, and sustainable manner. 29.

Article 95

1. The Regency Regional Government has the authority to administer the Gender and Children Data System in the Regency Area.
2. Administration of the Gender and Children Data System in the Regency Area as referred to in paragraph (1) is implemented in order to support development of Women's Empowerment and child protection in the Regency Area.
3. Preparation of the Gender and Children Data System as referred to in paragraph (1) becomes the basis for preparing Disaggregated Data related to the conditions and situations of women and men in various development sectors.
4. Disaggregated Data between women and men as referred to in paragraph (3) must be provided by each Regional Apparatus.
5. Collection and management of Disaggregated Data is implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations and is coordinated and published by the Regency Regional Apparatus that carries out governmental affairs in the field of communication and informatics.

Article 44

1. Achievement of provision of services for women victims of Violence requiring coordination in the Regency Area as referred to in Article 37 letter b shall be measured by criteria.
2. Criteria for provision of services as referred to in paragraph (1) shall include:
a. UPTD PPA that meets Service Standards for protection of women and Children; and
b. increased coverage of women victims of Violence who are served comprehensively in accordance with the needs of victims of Violence.

Article 65

The provisions regarding the protection of Women as Witnesses and/or Victims as referred to in Article 27 through Article 29 apply mutatis mutandis to the protection of children as Witnesses and/or Victims as referred to in Article 63 letter b.

I. GENERAL

Women and children have an important and strategic role in efforts to support development and the administration of regional government, however in reality the position of women and children in social, national and state life is still positioned as a group vulnerable to various forms of violence and/or threats of violence as well as other discriminatory treatment.

Women's Empowerment and Child Protection constitute the main pillars in efforts to improve the quality of reliable human resources in the future, by instilling and implementing the values of gender equality, and the implementation of the fulfillment of the rights of women and children, as well as enhancing the role and position of women and children in efforts to support the administration of government and development in the Region.

In the context of administering regional government affairs, women's empowerment and child protection, and improvement of family quality in the Sumedang Regency Area, is essentially one of the implementations of the administration of concurrent government affairs which are the authority of the Sumedang Regency Area in the field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

The Policy on Women's Empowerment and Protection, Child Protection, and Family Quality Improvement in the Sumedang Regency Area is implemented by involving and/or being supported by all components of society and stakeholders in the Sumedang Regency Area from various sectors of community life, and every program and activity is carried out comprehensively, in an integrated, sustainable, and continuous manner, as well as in synergy with national policies and programs in the field of women's empowerment and protection, child protection and family quality improvement.

To provide guarantees of legal certainty and legal protection as well as to realize effectiveness, efficiency, optimization, accountability, transparency, and administrative order as well as to serve as a guideline in the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection in the Sumedang Regency Area, it is necessary to regulate and stipulate by Regional Regulation.

I. GENERAL

Women and children have an important and strategic role in efforts to support development and the administration of regional government, however in reality the position of women and children in social, national and state life is still positioned as a group vulnerable to various forms of violence and/or threats of violence as well as other discriminatory treatment.

Women's Empowerment and Child Protection constitute the main pillars in efforts to improve the quality of reliable human resources in the future, by instilling and implementing the values of gender equality, and the implementation of the fulfillment of the rights of women and children, as well as enhancing the role and position of women and children in efforts to support the administration of government and development in the Region.

In the context of administering regional government affairs, women's empowerment and child protection, and improvement of family quality in the Sumedang Regency Area, is essentially one of the implementations of the administration of concurrent government affairs which are the authority of the Sumedang Regency Area in the field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

The Policy on Women's Empowerment and Protection, Child Protection, and Family Quality Improvement in the Sumedang Regency Area is implemented by involving and/or being supported by all components of society and stakeholders in the Sumedang Regency Area from various sectors of community life, and every program and activity is carried out comprehensively, in an integrated, sustainable, and continuous manner, as well as in synergy with national policies and programs in the field of women's empowerment and protection, child protection and family quality improvement.

To provide guarantees of legal certainty and legal protection as well as to realize effectiveness, efficiency, optimization, accountability, transparency, and administrative order as well as to serve as a guideline in the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection in the Sumedang Regency Area, it is necessary to regulate and stipulate by Regional Regulation.

I. GENERAL

Women and children have an important and strategic role in efforts to support development and the administration of regional government, however in reality the position of women and children in social, national and state life is still positioned as a group vulnerable to various forms of violence and/or threats of violence as well as other discriminatory treatment.

Women's Empowerment and Child Protection constitute the main pillars in efforts to improve the quality of reliable human resources in the future, by instilling and implementing the values of gender equality, and the implementation of the fulfillment of the rights of women and children, as well as enhancing the role and position of women and children in efforts to support the administration of government and development in the Region.

In the context of administering regional government affairs, women's empowerment and child protection, and improvement of family quality in the Sumedang Regency Area, is essentially one of the implementations of the administration of concurrent government affairs which are the authority of the Sumedang Regency Area in the field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

The Policy on Women's Empowerment and Protection, Child Protection, and Family Quality Improvement in the Sumedang Regency Area is implemented by involving and/or being supported by all components of society and stakeholders in the Sumedang Regency Area from various sectors of community life, and every program and activity is carried out comprehensively, in an integrated, sustainable, and continuous manner, as well as in synergy with national policies and programs in the field of women's empowerment and protection, child protection and family quality improvement.

To provide guarantees of legal certainty and legal protection as well as to realize effectiveness, efficiency, optimization, accountability, transparency, and administrative order as well as to serve as a guideline in the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection in the Sumedang Regency Area, it is necessary to regulate and stipulate by Regional Regulation.

Paragraph (1)
Point a
What is meant by "Children in Emergency Situations" are Children who are in environmental situations that threaten and disrupt the life and livelihood of Children caused by natural, non-natural, and/or social factors.

Point c
What is meant by "Children from Minority and Isolated Groups" are Children who are left behind, at the forefront, outermost in environments with different cultures, traditions, ethnicities, races, religions from other children whose numbers are far fewer than Children of other groups.

Point d
What is meant by "Children Who Are Economically Exploited" are Children who are victims of acts of prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or abilities of Children by other parties or other similar actions to obtain material benefits.

Point e

Point f

Point g
What is meant by "Children with HIV and AIDS" are Children who are infected with HIV and/or AIDS either transmitted from parents or from other risk factors.

Point h

Point k

I. GENERAL

Women and children have an important and strategic role in efforts to support development and the administration of regional government, however in reality the position of women and children in social, national and state life is still positioned as a group vulnerable to various forms of violence and/or threats of violence as well as other discriminatory treatment.

Women's Empowerment and Child Protection constitute the main pillars in efforts to improve the quality of reliable human resources in the future, by instilling and implementing the values of gender equality, and the implementation of the fulfillment of the rights of women and children, as well as enhancing the role and position of women and children in efforts to support the administration of government and development in the Region.

In the context of administering regional government affairs, women's empowerment and child protection, and improvement of family quality in the Sumedang Regency Area, is essentially one of the implementations of the administration of concurrent government affairs which are the authority of the Sumedang Regency Area in the field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

The Policy on Women's Empowerment and Protection, Child Protection, and Family Quality Improvement in the Sumedang Regency Area is implemented by involving and/or being supported by all components of society and stakeholders in the Sumedang Regency Area from various sectors of community life, and every program and activity is carried out comprehensively, in an integrated, sustainable, and continuous manner, as well as in synergy with national policies and programs in the field of women's empowerment and protection, child protection and family quality improvement.

To provide guarantees of legal certainty and legal protection as well as to realize effectiveness, efficiency, optimization, accountability, transparency, and administrative order as well as to serve as a guideline in the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection in the Sumedang Regency Area, it is necessary to regulate and stipulate by Regional Regulation.

I. GENERAL

Women and children have an important and strategic role in efforts to support development and the administration of regional government, however in reality the position of women and children in social, national and state life is still positioned as a group vulnerable to various forms of violence and/or threats of violence as well as other discriminatory treatment.

Women's Empowerment and Child Protection constitute the main pillars in efforts to improve the quality of reliable human resources in the future, by instilling and implementing the values of gender equality, and the implementation of the fulfillment of the rights of women and children, as well as enhancing the role and position of women and children in efforts to support the administration of government and development in the Region.

In the context of administering regional government affairs, women's empowerment and child protection, and improvement of family quality in the Sumedang Regency Area, is essentially one of the implementations of the administration of concurrent government affairs which are the authority of the Sumedang Regency Area in the field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

The Policy on Women's Empowerment and Protection, Child Protection, and Family Quality Improvement in the Sumedang Regency Area is implemented by involving and/or being supported by all components of society and stakeholders in the Sumedang Regency Area from various sectors of community life, and every program and activity is carried out comprehensively, in an integrated, sustainable, and continuous manner, as well as in synergy with national policies and programs in the field of women's empowerment and protection, child protection and family quality improvement.

To provide guarantees of legal certainty and legal protection as well as to realize effectiveness, efficiency, optimization, accountability, transparency, and administrative order as well as to serve as a guideline in the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection in the Sumedang Regency Area, it is necessary to regulate and stipulate by Regional Regulation.

Point a
What is meant by "Children in Emergency Situations" are Children who are in environmental situations that threaten and disrupt the life and livelihood of Children caused by natural, non-natural, and/or social factors.

Point b
What is meant by "Children in Conflict with the Law" are Children in conflict with the law, Children who are victims of criminal acts, and Children who are witnesses to criminal acts.

Point c
What is meant by "Children from Minority and Isolated Groups" are Children who are left behind, at the forefront, outermost in environments with different cultures, traditions, ethnicities, races, religions from other children whose numbers are far fewer than Children of other groups.

Point d
What is meant by "Children Who Are Economically Exploited" are Children who are victims of acts of prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or abilities of Children by other parties or other similar actions to obtain material benefits.

What is meant by "Children Who Are Sexually Exploited" are Children who are exploited to obtain benefits through sexual organs or other body organs of Children, including but not limited to all prostitution and indecency activities.

Point e
What is meant by "Children Who Are Victims of Narcotics, Alcohol, Psychotropic, and Other Addictive Substances Abuse" are Children who are persuaded, deceived, tricked, forced, and/or threatened to use narcotics, alcohol, psychotropics, and other addictive substances.

Point f
What is meant by "Children Who Are Victims of Pornography" are Children who experience trauma or suffering as a result of pornography crimes.

Point g
What is meant by "Children with HIV and AIDS" are Children who are infected with HIV and/or AIDS either transmitted from parents or from other risk factors.

Point h
What is meant by "Child Victims of Kidnapping" are Children who are taken by someone unlawfully with the intention of placing the Child under their power or the power of others or to place the Child in a helpless state.

What is meant by "Child Victims of Sale" are Children who are transferred by a person or group of people to other parties for compensation or other reasons.

What is meant by "Child Victims of Trafficking" are Children who experience psychological, mental, physical, sexual, economic, and/or social suffering resulting from acts of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt with threats of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether conducted within the country or internationally, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the Child being exploited.

Point i
What is meant by "Child Victims of Physical Violence" are Children who experience violence that causes pain, illness, or serious injury.

What is meant by "Child Victims of Psychological Violence" are Children who experience fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness, and/or severe psychological suffering.

Point j
What is meant by "Child Victims of Sexual Crimes" are Children who experience forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural and/or unwanted manner, and forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or specific purposes.

Point k
What is meant by "Child Victims of Terrorism Networks" are Children who experience physical, mental suffering, and/or economic loss caused by terrorism crimes whether as child victims, child perpetrators, children of perpetrators, and child witnesses.

Point 1
What is meant by "Children with Disabilities" are Children who experience physical, intellectual, mental, and/or sensory limitations over a long period of time who in interacting with the environment may experience obstacles and difficulties to participate fully and effectively based on equal rights.

Point m
What is meant by "Child Victims of Maltreatment" are Children who are threatened physically and non-physically due to acts of violence, treated wrongly or improperly in the family environment or closest social environment, so that their basic needs are not properly fulfilled either physically, spiritually, or socially.

Point n
What is meant by "Child Victims of Maltreatment" are Children who are threatened physically and non-physically due to acts of violence, treated wrongly or improperly in the family environment or closest social environment, so that their basic needs are not properly fulfilled either physically, spiritually, or socially.

What is meant by Child Victims of Neglect are Children who do not receive fulfillment of needs such as but not limited to health, security, and welfare needs from parents or other persons who have legal responsibility to care for the Child resulting in harm to the Child's growth and development process.

Point o

I. GENERAL

Women and children have an important and strategic role in efforts to support development and the administration of regional government, however in reality the position of women and children in social, national and state life is still positioned as a group vulnerable to various forms of violence and/or threats of violence as well as other discriminatory treatment.

Women's Empowerment and Child Protection constitute the main pillars in efforts to improve the quality of reliable human resources in the future, by instilling and implementing the values of gender equality, and the implementation of the fulfillment of the rights of women and children, as well as enhancing the role and position of women and children in efforts to support the administration of government and development in the Region.

In the context of administering regional government affairs, women's empowerment and child protection, and improvement of family quality in the Sumedang Regency Area, is essentially one of the implementations of the administration of concurrent government affairs which are the authority of the Sumedang Regency Area in the field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

The Policy on Women's Empowerment and Protection, Child Protection, and Family Quality Improvement in the Sumedang Regency Area is implemented by involving and/or being supported by all components of society and stakeholders in the Sumedang Regency Area from various sectors of community life, and every program and activity is carried out comprehensively, in an integrated, sustainable, and continuous manner, as well as in synergy with national policies and programs in the field of women's empowerment and protection, child protection and family quality improvement.

To provide guarantees of legal certainty and legal protection as well as to realize effectiveness, efficiency, optimization, accountability, transparency, and administrative order as well as to serve as a guideline in the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection in the Sumedang Regency Area, it is necessary to regulate and stipulate by Regional Regulation.

I. GENERAL

Women and children have an important and strategic role in efforts to support development and the administration of regional government, however in reality the position of women and children in social, national and state life is still positioned as a group vulnerable to various forms of violence and/or threats of violence as well as other discriminatory treatment.

Women's Empowerment and Child Protection constitute the main pillars in efforts to improve the quality of reliable human resources in the future, by instilling and implementing the values of gender equality, and the implementation of the fulfillment of the rights of women and children, as well as enhancing the role and position of women and children in efforts to support the administration of government and development in the Region.

In the context of administering regional government affairs, women's empowerment and child protection, and improvement of family quality in the Sumedang Regency Area, is essentially one of the implementations of the administration of concurrent government affairs which are the authority of the Sumedang Regency Area in the field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

The Policy on Women's Empowerment and Protection, Child Protection, and Family Quality Improvement in the Sumedang Regency Area is implemented by involving and/or being supported by all components of society and stakeholders in the Sumedang Regency Area from various sectors of community life, and every program and activity is carried out comprehensively, in an integrated, sustainable, and continuous manner, as well as in synergy with national policies and programs in the field of women's empowerment and protection, child protection and family quality improvement.

To provide guarantees of legal certainty and legal protection as well as to realize effectiveness, efficiency, optimization, accountability, transparency, and administrative order as well as to serve as a guideline in the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection in the Sumedang Regency Area, it is necessary to regulate and stipulate by Regional Regulation.

I. GENERAL

Women and children have an important and strategic role in efforts to support development and the administration of regional government, however in reality the position of women and children in social, national and state life is still positioned as a group vulnerable to various forms of violence and/or threats of violence as well as other discriminatory treatment.

Women's Empowerment and Child Protection constitute the main pillars in efforts to improve the quality of reliable human resources in the future, by instilling and implementing the values of gender equality, and the implementation of the fulfillment of the rights of women and children, as well as enhancing the role and position of women and children in efforts to support the administration of government and development in the Region.

In the context of administering regional government affairs, women's empowerment and child protection, and improvement of family quality in the Sumedang Regency Area, is essentially one of the implementations of the administration of concurrent government affairs which are the authority of the Sumedang Regency Area in the field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

The Policy on Women's Empowerment and Protection, Child Protection, and Family Quality Improvement in the Sumedang Regency Area is implemented by involving and/or being supported by all components of society and stakeholders in the Sumedang Regency Area from various sectors of community life, and every program and activity is carried out comprehensively, in an integrated, sustainable, and continuous manner, as well as in synergy with national policies and programs in the field of women's empowerment and protection, child protection and family quality improvement.

To provide guarantees of legal certainty and legal protection as well as to realize effectiveness, efficiency, optimization, accountability, transparency, and administrative order as well as to serve as a guideline in the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection in the Sumedang Regency Area, it is necessary to regulate and stipulate by Regional Regulation.

I. GENERAL

Women and children have an important and strategic role in efforts to support development and the administration of regional government, however in reality the position of women and children in social, national and state life is still positioned as a group vulnerable to various forms of violence and/or threats of violence as well as other discriminatory treatment.

Women's Empowerment and Child Protection constitute the main pillars in efforts to improve the quality of reliable human resources in the future, by instilling and implementing the values of gender equality, and the implementation of the fulfillment of the rights of women and children, as well as enhancing the role and position of women and children in efforts to support the administration of government and development in the Region.

In the context of administering regional government affairs, women's empowerment and child protection, and improvement of family quality in the Sumedang Regency Area, is essentially one of the implementations of the administration of concurrent government affairs which are the authority of the Sumedang Regency Area in the field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

The Policy on Women's Empowerment and Protection, Child Protection, and Family Quality Improvement in the Sumedang Regency Area is implemented by involving and/or being supported by all components of society and stakeholders in the Sumedang Regency Area from various sectors of community life, and every program and activity is carried out comprehensively, in an integrated, sustainable, and continuous manner, as well as in synergy with national policies and programs in the field of women's empowerment and protection, child protection and family quality improvement.

To provide guarantees of legal certainty and legal protection as well as to realize effectiveness, efficiency, optimization, accountability, transparency, and administrative order as well as to serve as a guideline in the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection in the Sumedang Regency Area, it is necessary to regulate and stipulate by Regional Regulation.

c. strengthening and development of Women's Protection Service Provider Institutions in the Regency Area.

Paragraph (1)
Point a
What is meant by "Children in Emergency Situations" are Children who are in environmental situations that threaten and disrupt the life and livelihood of Children caused by natural, non-natural, and/or social factors.

Point b
What is meant by "Children in Conflict with the Law" are Children in conflict with the law, Children who are victims of criminal acts, and Children who are witnesses to criminal acts.

Point c
What is meant by "Children from Minority and Isolated Groups" are Children who are left behind, at the forefront, outermost in environments with different cultures, traditions, ethnicities, races, religions from other children whose numbers are far fewer than Children of other groups.

Point d
What is meant by "Children Who Are Economically Exploited" are Children who are victims of acts of prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or abilities of Children by other parties or other similar actions to obtain material benefits.

What is meant by "Children Who Are Sexually Exploited" are Children who are exploited to obtain benefits through sexual organs or other body organs of Children, including but not limited to all prostitution and indecency activities.

Point e
What is meant by "Children Who Are Victims of Narcotics, Alcohol, Psychotropic, and Other Addictive Substances Abuse" are Children who are persuaded, deceived, tricked, forced, and/or threatened to use narcotics, alcohol, psychotropics, and other addictive substances.

Point f
What is meant by "Children Who Are Victims of Pornography" are Children who experience trauma or suffering as a result of pornography crimes.

Point g
What is meant by "Children with HIV and AIDS" are Children who are infected with HIV and/or AIDS either transmitted from parents or from other risk factors.

Point h

What is meant by "Child Victims of Trafficking" are Children who experience psychological, mental, physical, sexual, economic, and/or social suffering resulting from acts of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt with threats of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether conducted within the country or internationally, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the Child being exploited.

Point i
What is meant by "Child Victims of Physical Violence" are Children who experience violence that causes pain, illness, or serious injury.

Point n
What is meant by "Child Victims of Maltreatment" are Children who are threatened physically and non-physically due to acts of violence, treated wrongly or improperly in the family environment or closest social environment, so that their basic needs are not properly fulfilled either physically, spiritually, or socially.

I. GENERAL

Women and children have an important and strategic role in efforts to support development and the administration of regional government, however in reality the position of women and children in social, national and state life is still positioned as a group vulnerable to various forms of violence and/or threats of violence as well as other discriminatory treatment.

Women's Empowerment and Child Protection constitute the main pillars in efforts to improve the quality of reliable human resources in the future, by instilling and implementing the values of gender equality, and the implementation of the fulfillment of the rights of women and children, as well as enhancing the role and position of women and children in efforts to support the administration of government and development in the Region.

In the context of administering regional government affairs, women's empowerment and child protection, and improvement of family quality in the Sumedang Regency Area, is essentially one of the implementations of the administration of concurrent government affairs which are the authority of the Sumedang Regency Area in the field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

The Policy on Women's Empowerment and Protection, Child Protection, and Family Quality Improvement in the Sumedang Regency Area is implemented by involving and/or being supported by all components of society and stakeholders in the Sumedang Regency Area from various sectors of community life, and every program and activity is carried out comprehensively, in an integrated, sustainable, and continuous manner, as well as in synergy with national policies and programs in the field of women's empowerment and protection, child protection and family quality improvement.

To provide guarantees of legal certainty and legal protection as well as to realize effectiveness, efficiency, optimization, accountability, transparency, and administrative order as well as to serve as a guideline in the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection in the Sumedang Regency Area, it is necessary to regulate and stipulate by Regional Regulation.

Article 1

Article 62

Paragraph (1)
Point a
What is meant by "Children in Emergency Situations" are Children who are in environmental situations that threaten and disrupt the life and livelihood of Children caused by natural, non-natural, and/or social factors.

Point b
What is meant by "Children in Conflict with the Law" are Children in conflict with the law, Children who are victims of criminal acts, and Children who are witnesses to criminal acts.

Point c
What is meant by "Children from Minority and Isolated Groups" are Children who are left behind, at the forefront, outermost in environments with different cultures, traditions, ethnicities, races, religions from other children whose numbers are far fewer than Children of other groups.

Point d
What is meant by "Children Who Are Economically Exploited" are Children who are victims of acts of prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or abilities of Children by other parties or other similar actions to obtain material benefits.

What is meant by "Children Who Are Sexually Exploited" are Children who are exploited to obtain benefits through sexual organs or other body organs of Children, including but not limited to all prostitution and indecency activities.

Point e
What is meant by "Children Who Are Victims of Narcotics, Alcohol, Psychotropic, and Other Addictive Substances Abuse" are Children who are persuaded, deceived, tricked, forced, and/or threatened to use narcotics, alcohol, psychotropics, and other addictive substances.

Point f
What is meant by "Children Who Are Victims of Pornography" are Children who experience trauma or suffering as a result of pornography crimes.

Point g
What is meant by "Children with HIV and AIDS" are Children who are infected with HIV and/or AIDS either transmitted from parents or from other risk factors.

Point h
What is meant by "Child Victims of Kidnapping" are Children who are taken by someone unlawfully with the intention of placing the Child under their power or the power of others or to place the Child in a helpless state.

What is meant by "Child Victims of Sale" are Children who are transferred by a person or group of people to other parties for compensation or other reasons.

What is meant by "Child Victims of Trafficking" are Children who experience psychological, mental, physical, sexual, economic, and/or social suffering resulting from acts of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt with threats of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether conducted within the country or internationally, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the Child being exploited.

Point i
What is meant by "Child Victims of Physical Violence" are Children who experience violence that causes pain, illness, or serious injury.

What is meant by "Child Victims of Psychological Violence" are Children who experience fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness, and/or severe psychological suffering.

Point j
What is meant by "Child Victims of Sexual Crimes" are Children who experience forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural and/or unwanted manner, and forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or specific purposes.

Point k
What is meant by "Child Victims of Terrorism Networks" are Children who experience physical, mental suffering, and/or economic loss caused by terrorism crimes whether as child victims, child perpetrators, children of perpetrators, and child witnesses.

Point 1
What is meant by "Children with Disabilities" are Children who experience physical, intellectual, mental, and/or sensory limitations over a long period of time who in interacting with the environment may experience obstacles and difficulties to participate fully and effectively based on equal rights.

Point m
What is meant by "Child Victims of Maltreatment" are Children who are threatened physically and non-physically due to acts of violence, treated wrongly or improperly in the family environment or closest social environment, so that their basic needs are not properly fulfilled either physically, spiritually, or socially.

Point n
What is meant by "Child Victims of Maltreatment" are Children who are threatened physically and non-physically due to acts of violence, treated wrongly or improperly in the family environment or closest social environment, so that their basic needs are not properly fulfilled either physically, spiritually, or socially.

What is meant by Child Victims of Neglect are Children who do not receive fulfillment of needs such as but not limited to health, security, and welfare needs from parents or other persons who have legal responsibility to care for the Child resulting in harm to the Child's growth and development process.

Point o
What is meant by "Children Who Are Victims of Stigmatization from Labeling related to Their Parents' Condition" are Children who are given negative social labels based on prejudice and aimed at separating, differentiating, discrediting, and ostracizing Children with bad marks or views from labeling related to their parents' condition.

Domestic Violence hereinafter abbreviated as KDRT is any act against a person, especially women, that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically, and/or household neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of freedom within the household sphere. 38. Discrimination is any restriction, harassment, or exclusion that is directly or indirectly based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, group, class, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs, which results in reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural and other aspects of life. 39. Exploitation is an action with or without the victim's consent which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or service, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial. 40. Witness and/or Victim is a witness who is also a victim who experiences psychological, mental, physical, sexual, economic, and/or social suffering, caused by the criminal act of human trafficking. 41. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or adoptive mother. 42. Guardian is a person or body who in fact exercises custody as a Parent over a Child. 43. Business World is micro enterprises, small enterprises, medium enterprises, and large enterprises that conduct economic activities in Indonesia and are domiciled in Indonesia. 44. Community is individuals, families, groups, mass media, business world, and social organizations and/or community organizations. 45.
